chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"When you intend to depart on the day of Eid, and the dawn has broken while you are in the town, do not go out until you have performed the Eid prayer."

key_terms.الشُّخُوصَ: Departure or setting out on a journey
key_terms.تَشْهَدَ: To witness/attend (specifically referring to attending the prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they intend to travel on Eid day and dawn breaks before leaving?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the priority of communal Eid prayer over the convenience of early travel, emphasizing the social and spiritual significance of gathering with the community. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the obligation (or strong recommendation depending on the school of thought) to attend the Eid prayer even when it necessitates delaying departure, thereby reinforcing the unity of the believers. The hadith highlights the balance between individual logistical needs and collective religious observance.
